Your first PC build: a practical roadmap

Tech Compass · Updated 2026-10-19

IN THIS GUIDE

The quick answer1. Plan the whole system2. Check every fit3. Prepare a safe workspace4. Assemble using the manuals5. Check before first power6. Install and verifyFurther reading
THE QUICK ANSWER

Start with the work you need the computer to do, then choose compatible parts. Build from the component manuals, check each connection, and leave software installation until the hardware passes its first startup.

1. Plan the whole system

List your software requirements and budget. You will need a compatible CPU, motherboard, memory, storage, power supply, case, and cooling. Add a graphics card when your workload requires one or the processor lacks suitable integrated graphics.

2. Check every fit

Confirm the motherboard supports the CPU and its required firmware. Check memory generation, cooler mounting, case dimensions, GPU clearance, and power connectors. A parts list is not complete until these constraints agree.

3. Prepare a safe workspace

Work on a clean, dry, non-carpeted surface. Follow anti-static precautions in your component manuals. Keep power disconnected while assembling. Never open the power supply or reuse modular power cables from another supply unless the manufacturer confirms compatibility.

4. Assemble using the manuals

Fit the CPU without force, install memory in the recommended slots, and install storage. Fit the cooler following its thermal-paste instructions. Mount the board on the correct case standoffs. Connect the power supply, case controls, fans, and graphics card as required.

5. Check before first power

Check that no loose screws remain, all required power connectors are seated, and fans can rotate freely. Connect a display to the correct graphics output. On first startup, enter firmware setup and check that the expected memory and storage are detected.

6. Install and verify

Install a supported operating system from its official installation media, then updates and manufacturer drivers. Test normal workloads and monitor for stability. If the system fails to start, power off and use the motherboard’s documented diagnostic indicators.

What is a motherboard?

The motherboard is the main circuit board that connects the processor, memory, storage, and other components. Its connections determine which parts can work together.

What is a GPU?

A GPU is a processor designed to perform many calculations in parallel. It creates graphics for your screen and can also accelerate suitable computing tasks.

What is an operating system?

An operating system manages a device’s hardware and gives applications a common set of services. Windows, macOS, Linux distributions, Android, and iOS are familiar examples.
